name: Romania
headline_status: Cannabis is illegal in Romania, possession for personal use can bring prison, and medical cannabis exists on paper but is not available in practice.
summary: Possessing cannabis for personal use in Romania is a criminal offence punishable by three months to two years in prison or a criminal fine, and convictions for personal possession have risen sharply in the past decade. A 2013 amendment allows medical use of cannabis derivatives with up to 0.2% THC, but no licences have been issued and patients have no working prescription route. In October 2026 three senators filed a bill to replace prison with fines for personal-use possession, which prosecutors at DIICOT have opposed.

penalties.value: Personal-use possession is punishable by three months to two years in prison or a criminal fine.

medical_since.value: 2013 amendment to Law 339/2005 allows medical cannabis derivatives with up to 0.2% THC, but the framework has never been put into operation.

medical_program.value: No active prescribing pathway or reimbursement; no licences for cultivation or manufacture have been granted. Sativex is available only by special import authorisation.

possession_limit.value: No legal amount; there is no threshold separating personal use from trafficking in current law or the 2026 reform bill.

tourists.value: Visitors are subject to the same criminal penalties as residents, and there is no legal way to buy or use cannabis.

timeline.event: Law 339/2005 amended to allow medical cannabis derivatives up to 0.2% THC

pending.item: Senate bill to replace prison with administrative fines (1,000–3,000 lei) for possessing, growing or preparing drugs solely for personal use, and to create supervised consumption spaces.
pending.status: Filed in the Senate in October 2026; opposed by DIICOT.

faq.a: No. Possessing cannabis even for personal use is a crime punishable by three months to two years in prison or a fine.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis legal in Romania?
faq.a: On paper, low-THC cannabis derivatives have been allowed since 2013, but no licences have been issued and patients cannot get prescriptions in practice.
A Senate bill filed in October 2026 would replace prison with fines for personal-use possession, but it has not passed and prosecutors oppose it.
